reason: The hypothesis directly restates the core finding of P3, P7, P11, and P14—that fast nanosegregation of principal elements to grain boundaries causes ductility loss in single-phase CrMnFeCoNi—and frames it as a prediction. The proposed intervention (varying strain rate and temperature to control segregation) and the predicted outcome (brittle intergranular fracture at high strain rate/low temperature) are explicitly described in P1, P8, P9, and P10 for a refractory HEA, and the mechanism is taken word for word from the earlier literature. The only new element is the specific falsification test design, but the core idea is a restatement of known results.
copied_elements: dislocation-driven segregation of principal elements to grain boundaries
segregation reduces grain boundary cohesion and causes intergranular cracking
higher strain rate/lower temperature promotes segregation, lower strain rate/higher temperature reduces it
use of APT to detect grain boundary segregation
use of fractography to distinguish intergranular vs transgranular failure
